title: Exponential of a 3x3 real skew-symmetric matrix: Rodrigues formula and the zero-angle stratum
expression_sketch: Let A be a 3 x 3 real skew-symmetric matrix with entries A_12=-c, A_13=b, A_23=-a (and opposite signs below the diagonal), and set theta = sqrt(a^2 + b^2 + c^2). The exponential map exp: so(3) -> SO(3) is given by Rodrigues's formula: if theta != 0 then e^A equals I_3 plus (sin(theta)/theta)*A plus ((1-cos(theta))/theta^2)*A^2, while e^{0_3} = I_3. An equivalent reconstruction replaces I_3 by cos(theta)*I_3 and A^2 by the Gram matrix B with B_ij equal to the product of the axis components (a,b,c). The written quotients sin(theta)/theta and (1-cos(theta))/theta^2 are undefined at theta = 0; that stratum is the separate identity e^0 = I, equivalently the entire continuations sinc(0)=1 and (1-cos)''(0)/2 = 1/2. Gallier--Xu Theorem 2.2 extends the same trigonometric reconstruction to any nonzero real skew-symmetric n x n matrix by a commuting family of so(n) generators B_i with B_i^3 = -B_i.
latent_structure: One MATRIX_FUNCTION, the exponential of a skew-symmetric generator, is reconstructed from sin and cos of the rotation angle together with A and A^2. The generic theta != 0 quotient and the identity at theta = 0 are one entire matrix function, not two Piecewise programs. Degeneracy is the zero eigenvalue of A of multiplicity 3 (equivalently theta = 0).

theta.note: theta = sqrt(a^2+b^2+c^2) as written by Gallier

function_domains.exp: Entire on C; primary matrix exponential of a real 3 x 3 matrix, restricted here to so(3).

nonzero_conditions.statement: The displayed quotient form uses theta != 0; the value at the zero matrix is the separate member e^{0_3} = I_3 (Gallier Lemma 2.3.3 / Lemma 1.7: 'if theta != 0, with e^{0_3} = I_3').
nonzero_conditions.label: DECLARED
nonzero_conditions.source: J. Gallier, Basics of Classical Lie Groups, Lemma 2.3.3, https://www.cis.upenn.edu/~cis6100/cis61011lie1.pdf; J. Gallier, Geometric Methods and Applications, Lemma 18.6 / Lemma 1.7

positivity_conditions.statement: theta = sqrt(a^2+b^2+c^2) is written as a Euclidean norm, hence theta >= 0 (Gallier Lemma 2.3.3).
positivity_conditions.label: DECLARED
positivity_conditions.source: J. Gallier, Basics of Classical Lie Groups, Lemma 2.3.3, https://www.cis.upenn.edu/~cis6100/cis61011lie1.pdf

analytic_domains.statement: A is any 3 x 3 real skew-symmetric matrix. Then e^A lies in SO(3) and is given by the displayed Rodrigues formulae (Gallier Lemma 2.3.3).
analytic_domains.label: DECLARED
analytic_domains.source: J. Gallier, Basics of Classical Lie Groups, Lemma 2.3.3, https://www.cis.upenn.edu/~cis6100/cis61011lie1.pdf

analytic_domains.statement: For a nonzero real skew-symmetric n x n matrix, n >= 3, Gallier--Xu Theorem 2.2 gives a unique commuting family B_i of skew-symmetric matrices with B = sum theta_i B_i, B_i B_j = 0 (i != j), B_i^3 = -B_i, and e^B = I + sum_i (sin(theta_i) B_i + (1-cos(theta_i)) B_i^2).
analytic_domains.label: DECLARED
analytic_domains.source: J. Gallier, D. Xu, Computing exponentials of skew-symmetric matrices and logarithms of orthogonal matrices, Internat. J. Robotics Automat. 17 (2002) 10-20, Theorem 2.2, http://mainline.brynmawr.edu/~dxu/206-2550-2.pdf

branch_conventions: theta denotes the Euclidean norm sqrt(a^2+b^2+c^2) >= 0, not a signed angle with a branch cut.
sin and cos are the real trigonometric functions on R; no complex principal-value convention is used in the cited lemmas.
exp is the primary matrix exponential (power series), which on so(3) lands in SO(3).

limit_domains.statement: The quotient form is stated for theta != 0; the zero-angle value is the separate identity e^{0_3} = I_3 written in the same lemma, not an unspecified limit (Gallier Lemma 2.3.3).
limit_domains.label: DECLARED
limit_domains.source: J. Gallier, Basics of Classical Lie Groups, Lemma 2.3.3, https://www.cis.upenn.edu/~cis6100/cis61011lie1.pdf

derived_conditions.statement: A^3 = -theta^2 A for this 3 x 3 skew-symmetric A, which is the Cayley--Hamilton reduction used to collapse the exponential series onto span{I, A, A^2} (Gallier proof sketch of Lemma 2.3.3 / Lemma 1.7: A^2 = -theta^2 I + B, AB = BA = 0).
derived_conditions.label: DERIVED
derived_conditions.source: J. Gallier, Geometric Methods and Applications, Lemma 1.7 proof sketch; Lemma 2.3.3

why_not_cse_lgg: The generic formula is a trigonometric linear combination of I, A, A^2; at theta = 0 those coefficients are 0/0. CSE will not merge the two strata or recognise sinc and (1-cos)/theta^2 as the entire reconstructions. LGG will not invent the so(3) reduction A^3 = -theta^2 A as a representation covering the identity.
proposer_leak_risk: Hide Rodrigues, sinc, so(3), rotation axis. Catalog members are the two displayed formulae (theta != 0 and e^0 = I) and the entries of a general 3 x 3 real skew-symmetric matrix.
notes: Do not insert a principal-logarithm cut or complex theta. The source writes A real skew-symmetric and theta as a real square root of a^2+b^2+c^2; that nonnegativity is DECLARED. Do not claim the n >= 4 Gallier--Xu formula as a limit of the 3 x 3 identity; it is a separate theorem in the same paper. Do not identify this with the interpolating-polynomial definition of a general primary matrix function.
